findings: Original ColorDescriptor::distance controls confirm asymmetry for equal color counts, self-score1, ignored frequency weights and FLT_MAX for an empty input. This is a ranking dissimilarity, not a symmetric metric or exact identity predicate.

Distance rejects color-count differences greater than2 before comparing values. With equal counts it computes nearest-color distances only from first input toward second; when counts differ it uses larger-to-smaller direction.

create clears descriptor only near final formatting. Unsupported grayscale input or too few retained samples return before clear; reusing a populated output object can preserve old descriptor. Typical reviewed scanner creates fresh ColorDescriptor; no stale scanner output reproduced.

Final create loop assigns desc.numColors=descIndex before incrementing descIndex. One emitted color leaves count0, and N emitted colors are reported as N-1, omitting final slot from distance. This is a static original-source observation; full OpenCV kmeans/generator not executed.

Generator drops dark samples, masks edges with ellipse, uses kmeans32 and center-weighted frequency. Spatial arrangement and discarded areas are not represented by final palette. README transform claims cannot establish image identity.

Mask loop multiplies channel by255 then shifts8 even inside the mask, slightly reducing nonzero intensities; cv::Mat rgb=cvImg is shallow unless conversion/resize reallocates, so caller data mutation is possible for a3-channel unscaled input. Actual OpenCV alias/runtime behavior unqualified.

Descriptor creation notes randomness for identical input and uses kmeans++ one attempt; no seed/deterministic corpus proof. Colors store quantized LUV and weights in native struct; prior raw-blob storage remains layout-dependent.
